headline: Guided Badlands Tours and Fossil Access
reservation: Entry to the park is generally open, but camping and specific guided fossil tours require advance booking through the Alberta Parks system. Access to the Natural Preserve section is restricted to guided groups only to protect paleontological resources.

days.title: Badlands and Bonebeds

stops.name: Visitor Centre and Museum
stops.detail: View reconstructed skeletons and learn about the diverse Cretaceous species found within the park boundaries.

stops.name: Trail of the Fossil Hunters
stops.detail: Walk to a preserved fossil dig site and see the remains of a Corythosaurus housed in a protective building.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes from Brooks; watch for wildlife on the prairie roads
days.note: Summer temperatures in the badlands can be significantly higher than in town.

days.title: Coulee Views and Cottonwoods
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the park campground

stops.name: Badlands Trail
stops.detail: Hike through the hoodoos and pinnacles to see the unique geological layers of the Red Deer River valley.

stops.name: Cottonwood Flats Trail
stops.detail: Walk through the riparian forest along the river to spot local bird species and distinct flora.

days.driving: Local park loop driving; allow 20 minutes for the scenic circuit
days.note: The clay-based soil becomes impassable and extremely slippery when wet.

days.title: Red Deer River Basin
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from the Visitor Centre

stops.name: Great Badlands Lookout
stops.detail: Take in the expansive panoramic view of the park's erosion patterns from the high plateau.

stops.name: Brooks Aqueduct
stops.detail: Visit this nearby National Historic Site to see the massive concrete structure that once transformed the regional agriculture.

days.driving: Allow 90 minutes for the return trip to Brooks and the aqueduct site
days.note: Check wind conditions as the prairie can experience sudden high gusts.

intel.title: Visitor Centre Capacity
intel.text: The main lot near the museum serves as the hub for all guided tours and interpretive trails. On busy summer weekends, overflow parking is utilized near the day-use area.

intel.title: Deep Coulee Outages
intel.text: Cell service is generally reliable at the park entrance and Visitor Centre but drops off quickly in the lower coulees. Download maps before descending into the badlands.

intel.title: Regional Supply Points
intel.text: Brooks is the primary location for full services including fuel and groceries. There are no gas stations within the park itself, only a small convenience store.

intel.title: Guided Tour Windows
intel.text: Fossil tours typically run from May through October; check the official booking portal for seasonal start dates. Off-season access is limited to self-guided trails outside the preserve.

intel.title: Preserve Restrictions
intel.text: Large portions of the park are designated as a Natural Preserve and are closed to the public except via guided programs. Foot traffic is strictly limited to marked trails to prevent erosion.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental in Medicine Hat or Calgary, then stock up on water and supplies in Brooks before heading to the park.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for paved park roads, but high-clearance is better for gravel secondary roads; check rental insurance for gravel coverage.
plan.goldenHour: Great Badlands Lookout for sunset when the sandstone layers turn deep orange.
